title: DeepSeek Raises 100 Billion RMB in Doubled Funding Round
summary:
Interest from investors exceeded the original goal for the Chinese developer's second investment cycle, leading to a final raise of about Rmb 100bn (approximately $15B). The fundraise's pre-money valuation remained flat at Rmb 500bn despite the amount raised being twice the starting Rmb 50bn target. This increased intake followed the release of a new model, though some deal participants suggest the expanded round serves to finalize a shareholder list before a public offering.

DeepSeek plans to list on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2027 and has hired CITIC Securities to manage the process. The company has asked investors to convert single-deal funds into blind-pool vehicles so that multiple limited partners count as a single shareholder on the exchange. Founder Liang Wenfeng now controls about 70% of the company, which needs tens of billions of dollars in additional capital through 2029 to acquire new compute clusters.

selectedTweets.bestBit: filling a shareholder list before an IPO filing, at a price it settled in July
selectedTweets.text:
DeepSeek's second funding round opened in July with a Rmb 50bn target. It is now nearing completion at about Rmb 100bn, according to deal participants cited by Caijing, the Beijing business magazine.

The pre-money valuation did not move. It stays at about Rmb 500bn, the figure set when the round opened.

A round that doubles without a price increase can be read two ways. One is demand. The other is allocation: the company is filling a shareholder list before an IPO filing, at a price it settled in July. I read this as allocation.

The evidence sits in three lines of the deal. The first is the price, and it is flat.

My latest FlashPoint sets the other two lines beside it: https://t.co/3U21LN1yBH

The demand reading of DeepSeek's second funding round has real support. Bloomberg's sources said investor interest exceeded the plan after DeepSeek's latest model release.

Bloomberg had already reported commitments of at least Rmb 80bn, with a final tally that could approach Rmb 100bn.

selectedTweets.bestBit: hired CITIC Securities to prepare a listing on Shanghai's STAR Market
selectedTweets.text:
Two parts of DeepSeek's second funding round have not appeared in English coverage so far: the wrapper on the money, and the fee behind it.

Reuters reported in September that DeepSeek hired CITIC Securities to prepare a listing on Shanghai's STAR Market, the exchange's board for technology companies. Caijing, the Beijing business magazine, and Bloomberg both put the listing in 2027.

With a listing in view, I read the wrapper as a listing question. The fee is a different question: what it costs to get in.

selectedTweets.text:
DeepSeek has asked investors to convert some of their single-deal funds into blind-pool vehicles, Caijing, the Beijing business magazine, reports.

A blind pool is a fund that raises money before its investments are chosen. It would count as one shareholder when the exchange adds up holders, Caijing's sources say. A single-deal fund can be looked through to its limited partners, the investors in that fund.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Beijing blocked the sale of Manus, an AI agent startup, to Meta. In October, CNBC wrote that Manus's new raise suggests investors "aren't deterred" by Beijing's order.

Both CNBC and Bloomberg also note the change in ownership. Neither sets the new structure against the old one, part by part.

Benchmark, the Silicon Valley venture firm, is gone.

I read the shape that survived the review as the more useful signal for the next Chinese-founded AI startup abroad.
